A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LWF research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. V1's appendix baseline comparison can be matched to its expanded main-text counterpart in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original LWF experiments on domain-specific QA, larger-model and multi-task settings, ablations, and appendix experiments on translation, multilingual QA and side effects.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds F-learning comparisons, Qwen2.5-1.5B evaluation and an empirical approximation-sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 revises the stated selection size from the top 1/Nu fraction of Dself to |DL|/7 samples when Nu=7, which differs for unequal dataset sizes. Self-generation, the confidence formula and periodic unlearning loss remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this written revision changed the implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five QA datasets, multi-task combinations, English-to-German/French/Turkish/Chinese translation, and multilingual gsm8k in English, Italian, Chinese, Spanish and Turkish. The Qwen addition changes the model setting, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds F-learning to the comparison containing vanilla fine-tuning, BSS, SRS and LWF-mixed. The BSS/SRS comparison already appeared in v1 Appendix D, Table 14; its relocation does not introduce those baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation with Qwen2.5-1.5B and a protocol comparing one through four update steps using unlearning-subset overlap. Existing Llama settings, prompts, evaluation metrics and stated training budgets are retained. Naming AdamW supplies previously undisclosed information rather than establishing an optimizer switch.

E4.justification: New Appendix F tests whether replacing the one-step approximation with two, three or four updates changes selected unlearning examples. Existing confidence-filtering and unlearning-schedule ablations, forgotten-task analyses and appendix side-effect cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 2 retains the same distributions across task and unlearning-rate combinations. The new subset-overlap percentages are sensitivity results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds F-learning results averaging 38.37 versus LWF-mixed's retained 40.91, Qwen relative gains of 0.17%–1.57%, and subset overlaps of 99.81%–99.91% for two through four updates (Tables 3, 15 and 16). Matched earlier benchmark, ablation and appendix results, including the result plots, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 3 changes the log-posterior Hessian expansion's prefactor from -1/2 to +1/2, correcting its sign. New Appendix D details the Taylor expansion, omitted constant and linear terms, and Fisher/one-step substitutions. The Gaussian assumption and final confidence formula remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the novelty wording from the first systematic exploration of graceful forgetting in generative language models to its use for enhancing pretrained models' learning plasticity. The limitations section drops its broad 'first framework' description. The central abstract and conclusion claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains F-learning's weaker average performance through setting mismatch, attributes smaller Qwen gains to stronger initial capabilities, and interprets subset stability as supporting one-step approximation adequacy. It also newly characterizes near-total accuracy drops as suggesting near-complete unlearning. Existing superficial-forgetting and computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 first identifies AdamW and supplies a source-code URL; existing hardware, learning rate, batch size, epoch budget and prompts are retained. Conversely, Section 4.6 removes the URL identifying the exact unsup-simcse-bert-base-uncased checkpoint, leaving the generic SimCSE citation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ni et al. (2024) and distinguishes its knowledge-editing approach from fine-tuning plasticity enhancement. It also adds Bourtoule et al. (2021) and Loshchilov and Hutter (2019). The duplicated Zhang 2023a/2023b entries identify the same existing survey, not additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites selected related-work, method, experimental and limitations passages, adds a Baselines subsection and acknowledgments, and reorganizes appendix material while retaining the main narrative structure. Author/contact information is updated. Section 4.6 introduces inconsistent percentage-point versus percentage wording.

P2.justification: The appendix baseline table moves into the main text with an added F-learning row, and two new tables present Qwen and approximation results. Figure 1 is lightly reformatted and its spelling corrected. Existing result graphics are retained but repositioned or resized; the two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency through the Equation 3 correction and supporting derivation, and strengthens validation with an additional comparator, model family and selection-sensitivity check. Optimizer and code-access documentation also improve. These gains are limited by the narrow overlap-based evidence, removal of the exact SimCSE checkpoint, and the new percentage-point wording inconsistency. The core empirical results remain unchanged.
